facts.text: Mount Dennis got its name from Loyalist shipbuilder John Dennis and his family who owned a Humber boatyard in the early 1800s.
In 1913 Kodak Canada moved its factory to Eglinton and Weston, creating the industrial hub known as Kodak Heights that employed most locals until 2005.
The former Kodak power plant burned 500 tonnes of coal daily before closing in 2006, after which air quality improved dramatically.
Mount Dennis’ library, 60 years old, reopened in 2013 after renovations, serving as a community hub.
In 2014 a public art piece called Nyctophilia appeared at Weston Road and Dennis Avenue, part of revitalization projects.
Mount Dennis station will become the westernmost terminus of Line 5 Eglinton and a GO Transit stop when it opens, linking the neighbourhood to downtown.
